Swap your abdiel second form with Juri Han from Street Fighter V, who got isekai'd (hopefully not hit by a truck) into Shin Megami Tensei V with the name Juliel.   

### Commissioner

This mod was commissioned to me by @Lukedo3001, Juri is his favorite SFV character, really nice working with him and the model was really fun to port into the game.  
  
### This mod features:

- Juri Han Mecha skin as Abdiel Second Form;
- Her name, portrait, icon and a lore were added.

### Known issues:*
  
*If you use any mod that alters Name, Lore, or demon Icon:*
  
The files where these items are located are "common files", meaning they are shared between all demons, so if someone changes the name of a demon for example they are changing a "list" that have the name of all demons.  
  
It's all ok until you put another mod that does the same, depending on the load order it will overwrite these files and only the ones from the other mod will be loaded, meaning the first demon mod you installed will have its changes on name, lore icon, etc reverted, but the model and any other non shared files will be intact.  
  
My way of remediating this was prefixing my mod with ZZ0 so it will load last, and overwrite any other common file, but only solves this mod's problem and creates another since it will overwrite all the other custom demons names to the default ones.  
  
You can solve this by diffing my mod with the original file, diff the other mod with the original file then apply the diff patches to the original file, with smttools.

Have fun!

Experimental runtime texture dumping and replacement for Tales of Berseria Remastered for PC. Drop in the DLL, put your DDS files in the mods folder, done. No archive unpacking, no repacking, no game file edits.   
  

* * *

#### How it works

The game loads all assets from packed containers at runtime. Velvet Forge hooks into the file loading pipeline using detours: when the engine requests a texture by name, the hook intercepts that call and loads the replacement file from disk instead of reading from the container. The engine receives the replacement data through its own normal load path and never knows the difference.   
  
For the dumper: enable it, play through the areas you want to mod, and every loaded texture is written to disk as a DDS file with its real internal name. There's also a name dumper for dumping files with [TLTools](https://github.com/DaZombieKiller/TalesOfTools).

* * *

#### Supported texture formats

The game uses three DDS formats depending on the texture type:

-   `BC3 / DXT5` - diffuse maps with alpha (most character and environment textures)
-   `BC1 / DXT1` - diffuse maps without alpha
-   `B8G8R8A8_UNORM` - uncompressed, used for some UI and special textures

To convert your source image, use [DirectXTex](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex):

texconv your\_image.png -y -f DXT5 -m 3 -nogpu
texconv your\_image.png -y -f DXT1 -m 3 -nogpu
texconv your\_image.png -y -f B8G8R8A8\_UNORM -m 3 -nogpu

If you are unsure which format a texture uses, dump it first and run: 

texdiag.exe info your\_texture.dds

Match the format of the original before replacing it.

* * *

#### Installation

1.  Extract the archive into the game's root folder (same folder as the .exe)
2.  Open `velvetforge.ini` and adjust any paths if needed, all folders are created automatically on first run
3.  Launch the game normally

By default, modded textures are loaded from `velvetforge/textures/` and dumps go to `velvetforge/dump/textures/`.  
  
To uninstall, remove the DLL and the `velvetforge/` folder.

* * *

#### Configuration

Key

Default

Description

`mods_folder`

`velvetforge/textures`

Folder to load replacement DDS files from. Created automatically.

`dump_folder`

`velvetforge/dump/textures`

Folder where dumped textures are written. Created automatically.

`dump_textures`

`0`

Set to 1 to dump all loaded textures to disk

`dump_names`

`0`

Set to 1 to write internal asset names to name\_db.txt

`hot_reload`

`1`

Placeholder, WIP.

`external_log`

`0`

Set to 1 to write a log file to disk

`log_path`

_empty_

Log path. If empty, defaults to velvetforge.log in the game folder.

`debug_verbose`

`0`

1 = object probe details, 2 = full hook trace for crash debugging

`debug_console`

`0`

Set to 1 to open a console window for live log output

* * *

#### Modding textures

1.  Set `dump_textures=1` in `velvetforge.ini`
2.  Launch the game and visit the areas containing the textures you want to replace
3.  Dumped DDS files appear in `velvetforge/dump/textures/`
4.  Edit them in Photoshop with the DDS plugin or any DDS-capable tool
5.  Save as PNG and convert to the same format as the source texture
6.  Copy edited files to `velvetforge/textures/`, keeping the same filename
7.  Set `dump_textures=0`, relaunch, done

* * *

#### Notes

If you run into a bug or crash, post in the comments and link to your log file (enable `external_log=1` and `debug_verbose=2` first). Tested on v.1.0.4.
